children: , the social-media and digital-advertising giant, slid approximately 1.2% to $570.90 Monday as Reuters spotlighted another crack in its advertising defenses. The outlet uncovered 39 Facebook and Instagram ads allegedly funneling Indian users toward malware built to steal banking credentials. Meta removed them after Reuters intervened.

The trap was simple and ugly. Adult-content images allegedly lured users into downloading Android files outside official app stores, putting banking PINs and one-time passwords at risk. India lost nearly $2.4 billion to cyber fraud in 2025. Meta's advertising standards already ban nudity, scams and deceptive promotions. The rules were clear. The screening failed.

Thirty-nine ads are a rounding error beside Meta's 3.6 billion daily users and $60.8 billion of second-quarter revenue. The valuation gap is harder to ignore: the chart puts the stock 32.47% below its $845.42 GF Value estimate. That discount may grab investors' attention, but scale cuts both ways. With impressions jumping 14% and average ad prices rising 12% last quarter, Meta's money machine is acceleratingand every weak checkpoint becomes more expensive.

title: Meta Falls as 39 Scam Ads Trigger India Crackdown
